Divide $\mathbf{O}$ into $T_{r}$ blocks $\mathbf{O}_{i},\dots,\mathbf{O}_{T_{r}}$ of size $B_{r}\times d$ each, divide $\ell$ into $T_{r}$ blocks $\ell_{i},\dots,\ell_{T_{r}}$ of size $B_{r}$ each, divide $m$ into $T_{r}$ blocks $m_{1},\dots,m_{T_{r}}$ of size $B_{r}$ each.
Load $\mathbf{K}_{j},\mathbf{V}_{j}$ from HBM to on-chip SRAM.
Load $\mathbf{Q}_{i},\mathbf{O}_{i},\ell_{i},m_{i}$ from HBM to on-chip SRAM.

Read $\mathbf{P},\mathbf{dP}$ from HBM, compute $\mathbf{dS}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ where $dS_{ij}=P_{ij}(dP_{ij}-\sum_{l}P_{il}dP_{il})$ , write $\mathbf{dS}$ to HBM.

figures.caption: Left: FlashAttention uses tiling to prevent materialization of the large $N\times N$ attention matrix (dotted box) on (relatively) slow GPU HBM. In the outer loop (red arrows), FlashAttention loops through blocks of the $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$ matrices and loads them to fast on-chip SRAM. In each block, FlashAttention loops over blocks of $\mathbf{Q}$ matrix (blue arrows), loading them to SRAM, and writing the output of the attention computation back to HBM. Right: Speedup over the PyTorch implementation of attention on GPT-2. FlashAttention does not read and write the large $N\times N$ attention matrix to HBM, resulting in an 7.6 $\times$ speedup on the attention computation.

Left: Forward + backward runtime of standard attention and FlashAttention for GPT-2 medium (seq. length 1024, head dim. 64, 16 heads, batch size 64) on A100 GPU. HBM access is the primary factor affecting runtime. Middle: Forward runtime of FlashAttention (seq. length 1024, head dim. 64, 16 heads, batch size 64) on A100 GPU. Fewer HBM accesses result in faster runtime, up to a point. Right: The runtime (for seq. length 4K) of block-sparse FlashAttention is faster than FlashAttention by a factor proportional to the sparsity.
Left: runtime of forward pass + backward pass. Right: attention memory usage.
Validation perplexity of GPT-2 small/medium using two implementations. We confirm that FlashAttention yields the same validation curves as the baseline implementation from HuggingFace.
Speedup over standard PyTorch attention at different sequence lengths, on A100.
Speedup over standard PyTorch attention at different sequence lengths, on A100, with head dimension 128.

Speedup over standard PyTorch attention at different sequence lengths, on T4. Top: Combined forward pass + backward pass. Bottom: Forward pass only.

equation_roles.describes: standard attention S = QK^T, P = softmax(S), O = PV
numerically stable softmax via m(x), f(x), l(x)
decomposition of softmax over a concatenation: m, f, l of the whole from the halves
block sizes B_c = ceil(M/4d), B_r = min(ceil(M/4d), d)
running statistics update m_new, l_new with the rescale factors e^{m_i - m_new}
output update O_i <- diag(l_new)^{-1}(diag(l_i) e^{m_i-m_new} O_i + e^{m~-m_new} P~ V_j)
O(N^2 d) FLOPs, O(N) extra memory

no exact algorithm with o(N^2 d^2 M^{-1}) accesses for all M in [d, Nd]

D_i = P_i:^T dP_i: = do_i^T o_i (softmax backward without an N-length reduction)
backward recomputes P_ij = diag(l_i)^{-1} exp(S_ij - m_i) on chip

findings.question: Does FlashAttention beat the MLPerf 1.1 BERT-large record?
findings.setting: BERT-large, seq 512, 8xA100, 10 runs, to 72.0% MLM accuracy

findings.question: End-to-end GPT-2 training speedup vs HuggingFace and Megatron-LM?
findings.value: small: 2.7 d (3.5x vs HF 9.5 d; Megatron 4.7 d); medium: 6.9 d (3.0x vs HF 21.0 d; Megatron 11.5 d); ppl 18.2/14.3 unchanged
findings.note: Abstract says '3x speedup on GPT-2'; the Table 2 small-model row prints 3.5x. Text says 1.7x vs Megatron, the §4 bullet says 1.8x.

findings.question: Speed and accuracy on Long-Range Arena vs exact and approximate baselines?
Does 4x context still train faster than Megatron at 1K?
findings.value: FA 4K: 17.5 ppl, 3.6 d (1.3x) vs Megatron 1K: 18.2 ppl, 4.7 d; 0.7 ppl better, 30% faster

findings.question: Lift from longer sequences on MIMIC-III and ECtHR?
findings.note: '6.4 points of lift' in the abstract is the mean of 4.3 and 8.5.

findings.question: First Transformer above chance on Path-X / Path-256?
findings.setting: LRA Path-X (16K) and Path-256 (64K), pretrained on Path-64
findings.value: FlashAttention Path-X 61.4, Path-256 ✗; block-sparse Path-X 56.0, Path-256 63.1; all baselines ✗

findings.question: Runtime and memory of the attention kernel alone vs baselines?
findings.setting: one A100 40GB, dropout + padding mask, seq 128..64K
findings.value: up to 3x faster than PyTorch attention for 128-2K; approximate methods cross over between 512 and 1024; memory linear in N, up to 20x less than exact baselines, 2x less than Linformer at 64K

findings.question: Is HBM traffic, not FLOPs, what sets runtime?
findings.setting: GPT-2 medium attention fwd+bwd, seq 1024, d 64, 16 heads, batch 64, A100
findings.value: standard 66.6 GFLOPs / 40.3 GB / 41.7 ms; FlashAttention 75.2 GFLOPs / 4.4 GB / 7.3 ms

findings.question: How does speedup vary with GPU and head dim?
findings.value: A100 2-4x; A100 d=128 less (up to 3x with causal mask); RTX 3090 2.5-4.5x (lower HBM bandwidth ~900 GB/s vs 1.5 TB/s)
